My {{ls}}oul in Hel.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Corrupt tran{{ls}}lation again{{ls}}t the Article of Chri{{ls}}ts de{{ls}}cending into Hel.}}Where al the Faithful, according to the Creede, euer haue beleeued, that Chri{{ls}}t according to his {{ls}}oul, went downe to Hel, to deliuer the Patriarches and al iu{{ls}}t men there holden in bondage til his death, and the Apo{{ls}}tle here citing the Prophets wordes, mo{{ls}}t euidently expre{{ls}}{{ls}}eth the {{ls}}ame, di{{ls}}tingui{{ls}}hing his {{ls}}oule in Hel, from his body in the graue: Yet the Caluini{{ls}}ts to defend again{{ls}}t Gods expre{{ls}}{{ls}}e wordes, the bla{{ls}}phemie of their Mai{{ls}}ter, that Chri{{ls}}t {{ls}}uffered the paines of Hel, and that no where but vpon the Cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e, and that otherwi{{ls}}e he de{{ls}}cended not into Hel, mo{{ls}}t fal{{ls}}ely and flatly here corrupt the text, by turning and wre{{ls}}ting both the Hebrew and Greeke wordes {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=נפש ''{{lang|grc|ψυχὴ}}'' שאול ''{{lang|grc|ᾅδου}}''}}from their mo{{ls}}t proper and v{{ls}}ual {{ls}}ignifications of, ''Soule'', and ''Hel'', into ''body'', and ''graue'': {{ls}}aying for, ''my {{ls}}oule in Hel'', thus, ''my body'', {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* ''Eng. Bible. 1579''}}''life, per{{ls}}on'', yea (as Beza in his new Te{{ls}}tament an. 1556) ''my carcas'' in the ''graue''. and this later they corrupt almo{{ls}}t through out the Bible for that purpo{{ls}}e. But for refelling of both corruptions, it {{ls}}hal be {{ls}}ufficient in this place: fir{{ls}}t, that al Hebrues & Greekes, and al that vnder{{ls}}tand the{{ls}}e tonges, know that the fore{{ls}}aid Hebrue & Greeke wordes are as proper, peculiar, and v{{ls}}ual to {{ls}}ignifie, ''{{ls}}oul'' and ''Hel'', as ''anima'' and ''infernus'' in Latin, yea as ''{{ls}}oul'' and ''Hel'' in Engli{{ls}}h do properly {{ls}}ignifie the {{ls}}oule of man, and Hel that is oppo{{ls}}ite to heauen: and that they are as vnproprely v{{ls}}ed to {{ls}}ignifie body and graue, as to {{ls}}ay in English, {{ls}}oul for body, or Hel for graue. Secondly, it doth {{ls}}o mi{{ls}}like the Heretikes them {{ls}}elues, that Ca{{ls}}taleo one of their fine Tran{{ls}}latours refelleth it, and to make it the more {{ls}}ure, he for, ''in inferno'', tran{{ls}}lateth, ''in Orco'', that is, ''in Hel''. What neede we more? He oppo{{ls}}eth him {{ls}}elf both again{{ls}}t plaine Scriptures and al auncient fathers, peruerting the one, and contemning the other, to ouerthrow that truth which is an Article of our ''Crede''. Whereby it is euidently fal{{ls}}e which {{ls}}ome of them {{ls}}ay for their defen{{ls}}e, that none of them did euer of purpo{{ls}}e tran{{ls}}late fal{{ls}}ely.
